_about: getEndUser answers that the app's gate (backend/services/identity_lookup._cii_parse) and the Mac's persona self-check (deploy/lab5/lab5_cii.parse_end_user) must read the same way. expect: found (details, no error), not_found (CII's 'no such user': no error at all, and getEndUser null or a present, null endUserDetails), unavailable (anything else, every answer that carries an error included, whatever the error says). No error at all is errors absent, null or an empty list; any other errors value carries one, an empty object, an empty string, 0 or false included. An unavailable case may carry trust, failing and reasons: what a partial answer did say, which the gate keeps and still blocks on (reasons: its block; none: nothing against the user), while the self-check reads every unavailable answer as a failed query. If spikes S5/S6 show CII answers a login it has no record of with an error, that exact answer is added here as not_found and matched exactly in both copies, never by its words. Run by tests/test_identity_gate.py and tests/test_identity_personas.py.

error_messages._about: Messages of a code-less error, each tried in every shape below: on getEndUser (getEndUser null), on its endUserDetails (getEndUser an object, endUserDetails null), on getEndUser with data null (the shape the published schema gives such an error: getEndUser returns the non-null GetEndUserOutput!, so an error on it nulls the whole of data), and with no path (data null). Every one is unavailable, whatever it says: the first ones read like CII saying 'no such user', the rest are about something else (a permission, a scope, a role, a pool, a session, another principal). No error is ever read as that answer by its words.
